name.text: Points and the perpendicular bisector of AB

questiontext.text:
\(A\) is \(({@A[1]@}, {@A[2]@})\) and \(B\) is \(({@B[1]@}, {@B[2]@})\). The locus of points equidistant from \(A\) and \(B\) is drawn. For each point, decide where it is.

  1. \(P = ({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
  2. \(P = ({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
  3. \(P = ({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
  4. \(P = ({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
A point is on the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\) exactly when it is the same distance from \(A\) as from \(B\). Compare the squares of the distances, worked out by Pythagoras, so that nothing is rounded. The midpoint of \(AB\) is \(M({@M[1]@}, {@M[2]@})\), but \(AB\) is not horizontal or vertical, so the bisector is a sloping line through \(M\).

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@PA2[1]@}\) and \(PB^2 = {@PB2[1]@}\), so the point is [[if test="is(cats[1]=1)"]]on the locus[[elif test="is(cats[1]=2)"]]nearer to \(A\)[[else]]nearer to \(B\)[[/if]].

  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@PA2[2]@}\) and \(PB^2 = {@PB2[2]@}\), so the point is [[if test="is(cats[2]=1)"]]on the locus[[elif test="is(cats[2]=2)"]]nearer to \(A\)[[else]]nearer to \(B\)[[/if]].

  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@PA2[3]@}\) and \(PB^2 = {@PB2[3]@}\), so the point is [[if test="is(cats[3]=1)"]]on the locus[[elif test="is(cats[3]=2)"]]nearer to \(A\)[[else]]nearer to \(B\)[[/if]].

  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@PA2[4]@}\) and \(PB^2 = {@PB2[4]@}\), so the point is [[if test="is(cats[4]=1)"]]on the locus[[elif test="is(cats[4]=2)"]]nearer to \(A\)[[else]]nearer to \(B\)[[/if]].

questiondescription.text:
Loci: points and the perpendicular bisector

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.3: Decide whether a point is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, or nearer to A or to B, by comparing squared distances.

Core

This question is original to this project.
